comment: The kindest woman you'll meet at Richmond. Her FYS class is mostly reading, no papers during the year, and you just talk about the reading each class. Participation is very important. You will be graded on very few things, with the final 10-page paper being 30% of your grade after not writing any papers all semester.

reading heavy class!!! only a few things are graded we have one final paper and then other than that it's basically just a participation grade in the seminar style classes. prof is so nice tho she's just the sweetest

She is a sweet, knowledgeable professor who wants you to grow. The class is seminar-style based on the hw's; be ready to share your personal experiences and the hw readings as you dive into how people deal with loss. You will also have a free-write, speaker interview, and paper + presentation.

Dr. Skerrett is super kind and led a super interesting class. only thing is the only real grade the class had was a final project and essay on that project topic. she was a little bit of a tough grader so your grade relied on how well you did on the project.

Very sweet and engaging professor. I never imaged I would be taking a class of death and grieving, but she made it very interesting! Get ready to read because you read a new book almost every week. At the end of each class, you write in a journal. No essays all semester except for final essay. Main project is directing a group interview for speaker

I'm so glad I took Loss and Remains! The subject matter can be a bit heavy but Dr. Skerrett does an excellent job at handling it and turning grief into a lesson. Reading is required for success and there are 7 books used in the course in addition to a research paper, interview, and journal. Lectures can be a bit boring but nonetheless fruitful.

- Love Her
- Class setup is odd but you get used to it
- Very passionate about her work and truly cares about students
- Class readings are also good selections, especially if you are into legal work
- Super understanding 
- Grading is straightforward
- Paper revisions are allowed
- Decent amount of group work, but doable
- Overall, recommend it!
I took her FYS and it was just as an FYS should be.  Very focused on what you gave learned. You are allowed to revise papers.  Overall good class.

She is such a nice professor that she even reminds you to connect with your teammates when doing group projects. Her class is so welcome and warm for first-year students. Although with papers and readings, but not unbearable. Make use of the writing consultant for her class then you will pass. If you can't register other easy fys, take her class !

Dr Skerrett is an amazing professor. Lots of readings, but they are not extremely difficult. She only gives papers, but they are easy to do well on as long as you follow the prompt. She doesn't give grades back until the last week of classes, but lets you revise your work for a better grade.

Dr. Skerrett is really good! Yes you wont know your grade until the end of the semester, but she is still a very good professor. She brings in lots of interesting guest speakers, and asks you to read (a lot, but not unbearable especially with other reading heavy classes), but the books are also very interesting. Race and Law is a good FYS, take it!

Dr Skerret is very nice, but there was a lot of work and you will have no idea how you are doing in the class. We had 4 papers on 5 books over the semester, and I did not receive any grades until finals started. She is very smart, but I did not like the class setup.

Dr. Skerrett is a kind and likable professor who is easily accessible outside of class to help. But the class had a lot of reading and was graded by very few assignments; each assignment had no sort of grading criteria. She leaves a lot of comments on essays, but her handwriting is illegible so you need to go meet with her to get actual feedback.
